newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Taleban forces report more gains north of Kabul.
newsitem.headline: Taleban forces report more gains north of Kabul.

text.p: Heavy fighting continued for a second day on Monday on the front lines north of Kabul and commanders of the radical Islamic Taleban militia said they were still advancing.
"We advanced five kilometers (three miles) yesterday and our troops are still moving forward," Taleban commander Mohammed Usman told Reuters on Monday.
The Taleban launched a major offensive some 20 km (13 miles) north of Kabul on Saturday night against forces of the ousted government and their allies.
On Sunday morning jubilant Taleban fighters said they had taken the strategically important villages of Mir Bacha Kot and Gul Dara.
On Monday morning artillery commander Usman said he was unsure of the exact position of the front line as the Taleban continued to advance.
Usman was directing repeated salvos from a multiple rocket launcher from positions slightly behind the front line against the village of Qarabagh, 28 km (17 miles) north of the capital.
The opposition responded to the rocket fire with sporadic shelling of a Taleban-held village closer to the fighting.

The Taleban's recent advance has delivered it some ground lost to the alliance in mid-October. When the Taleban took Kabul on September 27, they pushed rapidly north, driving back the forces of the ousted government.

But the ex-government forces, bolstered by Uzbek General Abdul Rashid Dostum, counter-attacked, forcing the Taleban back to a low range of hills that bisect the broad valley that runs north of Kabul to the foothills of the Hindu Kush.
Repeated attacks by the opposition alliance, however, were unable to dislodge the Taleban from the line of hills, which is considered vital for the alliance's efforts to retake Kabul.
Afghan watchers in Kabul say the Taleban advances over the weekend will further weaken the opposition's chances of retaking the capital.
It was not possible to estimate the number of casualties suffered by either side in the battle.
The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) is airlifting medical supplies from Kabul to the opposition stronghold of Mazar-e-Sharif for casualties on the other side of the front line.

"We have sent 1,700 kilograms (1.7 tonnes) of medical material to Mazar-e-Sharif, from where it will travel by road to the (opposition base of the) Panjsher," said the ICRC's press officer in Kabul, Jean-Luc Paladini, referring to the alliance's Panjsher Valley stronghold.
"We have decided to take it by air because we could not cross the front line by road. The Taleban have given us the green light," said Paladini.
Paladini said the medical supplies included dressings, plasma and anaesthetics.
The ICRC gives medical supplies to all factions in the Afghan conflict.
